security.finding: /api/auth/test-login exists and mints a real platform_admin session. It is deleted from the build only on a Vercel production build (VERCEL=1 AND VERCEL_ENV/NODE_ENV=production); a Preview, self-hosted or container production build keeps it and relies entirely on four env-var gates plus a secret.

Neither auth backdoor writes an audit row. logBackdoorAttempt is a console.warn, so a successful platform_admin sign-in through /api/auth/test-login or /api/auth/verify-izzat leaves no in-product trace.
A second backdoor, /api/auth/verify-izzat (the simulation bridge), exists on the same pattern and the same non-auditing guard.
When no IP allow-list is configured, ALLOW_BACKDOOR_WITHOUT_IP_ALLOWLIST=true re-opens a backdoor in production that otherwise fails closed.

/api/sap/tdd/preview, /entities and /operations perform live customer-SAP reads with NO ApiAccessGrant check and NO audit row. The only gate is a session plus canAccessStudio (consultant or platform_admin).

/preview lets the caller choose tenant, service, entity and limit from the query string; /entities with ?probe=1 fans a live probe over every entity set a service exposes. Neither writes an audit row, so the traffic is invisible to the Operations console.

On the northbound WRITE path and in the Test Console dry run the caller-supplied entity overrides the governed Interface.entitySet (parsed.data.entity ?? iface.entitySet), the inverse of the read path's precedence. Validation is only z.string().max(200).
/api/sap/tdd/preview reads ?entity= straight from the query string and passes it to previewSapEntitySet with no grant and no audit.

Test Console Replay picks the credential whose environment matches the saved case; a case recorded before the environment was stored sends no clientId and the server refuses AMBIGUOUS_CREDENTIAL when more than one credential is live. Correct behaviour, stated here for the record.

broker-run applies the same RETIRED-solution gate as authenticateClientToken via the shared checkSolutionRuntime, so a RETIRED solution IS refused on both paths. RESTRICTED is deliberately not refused on either.

broker-run has no per-credential rate limit, unlike every /api/northbound route. It is covered only by the edge IP-keyed sapLive bucket, so one browser session can drive repeated live tenant reads at the IP ceiling.
broker-run does not touch lastUsedAt, so a console run does not show up as credential activity the way a real call does.
The admin layout gates on ["platform_admin","admin"], but "admin" is a LegacyUserRole and not a member of the UserRole union — a dead string in a role check.

The partial unique index SapConnection_active_binding_tuple exists only as hand-written SQL; prisma db push (which CI uses) does not create it, so a database provisioned that way can hold two indistinguishable ACTIVE connections and refuse every request for that environment as AMBIGUOUS.

capabilities.name: Scheduled per-lane health checks with a timestamped outcome and a TTL
capabilities.notes: A nightly cron probes every active connection, writes lastValidationStatus/lastValidatedAt and appends an append-only SapConnectionProbeEvent, alerting on the healthy-to-failing transition; the run itself is recorded in CronRunLog. Missing: the unit is the CONNECTION, not an interface or service lane; there is NO TTL — no code compares lastValidatedAt against a maximum age and no status decays to stale or unknown; a connection with no probe path is skipped and keeps its old status.

capabilities.name: Per-service health stored separately for metadata reachability vs data readability
capabilities.notes: The distinction is drawn in code (probeConnection measures $metadata reachability; readEntitySet separates OK from EMPTY; /operations computes reachable-but-empty explicitly) but only metadata reachability is PERSISTED against a connection. Data-readability facts live in a short-TTL request cache, in SapHubContent.rawMetadataJson.probes (deployment-scoped, keyed by tenantKey not connection), and in NorthboundAuditEvent.rowCount as a side effect of real traffic. Nothing joins them into a per-service health record.

capabilities.name: Correlation IDs: generated, stored, queryable by exact match, retained
capabilities.notes: Generated as randomUUID() first in every northbound handler, returned in the body and in an x-correlation-id header, and stored non-null on NorthboundAuditEvent. NOT queryable by exact match: there is no index on correlationId (only [organizationId,solutionId,at] and [organizationId,clientTokenId,at]) and no endpoint accepts it as a filter. NO retention: nothing deletes NorthboundAuditEvent anywhere in src, scripts or prisma.

capabilities.name: One-time claim link / token-scoped key delivery
capabilities.notes: A key is delivered in the HTTP response body of the issuing call, once, to whichever browser session pressed the button, and rendered with a Copy button. Only the SHA-256 hash of the read token is stored; the write key is sealed AAD-bound to its credential row. There is no claim link, no one-time-use URL, no expiring delivery token, no out-of-band channel and no per-recipient scoping.

capabilities.name: Rate limiting on the northbound routes
capabilities.notes: Two layers: an edge IP-keyed bucket in middleware (apiRead 300/min, apiMutation 120/min, sapLive 20/min) and a per-credential 60/min bucket inside each of the four northbound routes, with reads and writes on separate budgets. All four write a 429 audit row before refusing. Caveats: without UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/_TOKEN the limiter is a per-instance in-memory Map; on a Redis outage it fails closed in production; /api/studio/test/broker-run has no per-credential bucket.

capabilities.name: Circuit breaker or backoff around SAP calls
capabilities.notes: rg -in 'circuit|breaker|backoff|exponential|retries' over src/lib/northbound, src/lib/sap-public and src/lib/ops returns no matches. What exists is a per-call AbortController timeout (read 15s default / 30s max; probe 10s / 30s) and bounded sweep concurrency (SWEEP_CONCURRENCY=4). A failing tenant is called again on the very next request. The incident rules connection-unhealthy and upstream-errors observe the failure after the fact; they are a detector, not a breaker.

capabilities.name: SAP host allowlist validation on save, and where the connection secret is encrypted/decrypted
capabilities.notes: Validation is a DENY-list, not an allow-list: https is required and localhost/.local/.internal plus every IPv4 and IPv6 literal are refused, but any other https host may be saved — there is no positive list of SAP domains. The module's own header states that a public DNS name resolving privately is out of its reach. Encryption is AES-256-GCM keyed by SAP_CONNECTION_ENCRYPTION_KEY (64 hex chars, enforced), with AAD binding each ciphertext to its row (connectionAad for a connection, solutionClientRowAad for a credential; the superseded solutionClientAad is kept only to recognise and REFUSE a v1 blob). Exactly five call sites: encrypt at connection-resolver.ts:755 and write-credential.ts:71; decrypt at connection-resolver.ts:167 and write-credential.ts:108,149.

capabilities.name: Secret rotation with a probe before the stored secret is replaced
capabilities.notes: upsertSapConnection seals and writes in one upsert with no connectivity check anywhere in the path; the only failure the route can report is that SEALING failed. The audit row records secretsRotated: true regardless of whether the new secret works. Credential rotation likewise overwrites tokenHash immediately with a deliberate no-grace-period policy. probeConnection exists but is only reachable after the fact via the Studio test route, the Ops probe-now action, or the nightly sweep — so the sequence is save, then find out, and lastValidatedAt still shows when the OLD secret last returned 200.

capabilities.name: Write scope: a write path, what authorises it, and an approval record
capabilities.notes: POST /api/northbound/interfaces/[id]/data/write, behind eight gates in order: bearer client token, a SECOND secret (x-coreedge-write-key verified against this credential's row in constant time), a separate northbound-write throttle, a MANDATORY Idempotency-Key, body schema, resolveWritableInterface (ACTIVE WRITE interface plus a live unrevoked unexpired WRITE grant for this environment, evaluated at call time), a stricter connection binding that refuses an undeclared environment outright, and connection.writeEnabled as a per-tenant veto. The approval record is ApiAccessGrant, with segregation of duties (requestedById must differ from decidedById), a mandatory write checklist, a mandatory expiry on every granting decision, no re-decision of a settled grant, and revocation recorded as a second fact with a mandatory reason. There is no per-call confirmation by design; grant approval is the single human checkpoint.
